key_idea: Show that the Faltings–Zhang difference family of the universal curve is non-degenerate, meaning its Betti form has nonvanishing top power. This gives a height inequality on the total space of the abelian scheme, where the Néron–Tate height dominates the modular height. From that, points of a curve with large modular height are spread apart in Néron–Tate distance, so a Vojta–Rémond packing argument bounds the count by c^{1+ρ}.
reason: The strategy has a clear core idea: real-analytic Betti-map non-degeneracy feeds into intersection theory to give a height inequality, which in turn gives a uniform repulsion of points. Still, it needs a long chain of supporting pieces, including Betti forms, a graph construction, upper and lower intersection-number bounds, a Silverman–Tate estimate, an outsourced non-degeneracy theorem, packing lemmas, and a separate Northcott/Rémond argument for the case of small modular height.
recognized: Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger, 'Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves' (Annals of Math. 2021)
